entries.hypothesis: Canon mis-transcribes the dense OTP pages 45-54, where every prior audit was weakest.

entries.result: SETTLED, and canon is upheld. Pages 45-54 read at 1.0000 over 1,992 slots: zero substitution disagreements (0 SEG, 0 CONF, 0 ID) and zero surviving insertion/deletion candidates. The two indel flags raised on the dense stratum both adjudicate to SEG - non-rune ink inside the band on lines whose rune-body component count matches canon exactly. Why this worked where frontB did not: frontB forced a NUMBER OF PIECES and let the cuts fall where they may; T2 forces the IDENTITY SEQUENCE and lets the ink choose the cuts, so the segmentation never has to be discovered. frontB's own reported segmentation gap (30-41 boxes per line on p45 against canon's 21-25) was an artifact of not applying its own measured height classes as a mask: with the mask, rune-component counts are exact on 530/604 lines (87.7%) against R9's 232/604 (38.4%), residual 83 glyphs over 13,136 = 0.63%.

entries.result: REFUTED for random.org. It has published a 1 MiB true-random file every day since 2006-03-11 (7,395 files). 153 files covering 2013-09 to 2014-01 were downloaded and verified 153/153 against the published MD5s. NIST Beacon v1 also still serves the 2013 era via its legacy endpoint (the v2 API cannot - it clamps to chain 1 pulse 1, 2018-07-23). ANU QRNG and HotBits ARE unreachable, with cause: ANU's only pre-generated bundle died with CloudStor 2023-12-15, HotBits keeps no records by design.
entries.coverage: A measured source table replaces the assertion. See P2's RESULTS.md.
entries.not_covered: Dice and /dev/urandom remain genuinely closed - they leave no seed AND no record. The correction is that the census merged those two properties.

entries.hypothesis: The anti-repeat hardening was applied BY HAND by a human calligrapher (asserted as fact in FINAL-SYNTHESIS.md:73-76 and load-bearing for the attribution profile), rather than by a machine.
entries.threshold: Pre-registered per test, with matched controls: a machine-filtered stream, a human-like stream (lag-1..3 avoidance, alternation excess, window rebalancing) and an unfiltered uniform stream, all bisection-calibrated to the real 0.6638% doublet rate so lag-1 carries no information. Every claim reports its measured power.

control_detail.gate: uniform vs machine on lag1_z, power 1.000

entries.result: MACHINE. Every human-randomness model with any signature beyond the bare immediate-repeat rule is excluded at >=0.99 power. Pooled lag-2..8 bleed is z = +0.65 (zero bleed, and the sign is wrong for a human). The filter had NO per-line scope (power 1.000): 4/86 residual doublets cross a line boundary, 4.65% against a 4.58% base, where a line-scoped filter leaves 22.9%. BOUND: lag-1 suppression is 80.75%, and any lag-2..8 suppression above 1.70% is excluded at 95% (2.87% at 99%).
entries.coverage: Discriminates the SOURCE of the randomness. Reported as UNDERPOWERED (0.110) for the separate question of whether a human eye applied ONLY that one rule to a machine-generated pad - which is unfixable in principle, since such a stream IS the coded filter's output. Tests of drift, fatigue, per-page rate constancy and off-diagonal bigram structure are underpowered at n=12,956 (0.075-0.195) and are reported as such, not as evidence.
entries.not_covered: 'A person did the writing' is untouched; only 'a person supplied the randomness' is excluded.

(1) The pp49-51 images are deterministic 400-DPI Ghostscript renders of typeset text, so same-character glyphs are pixel-identical (measured within-class IoU 0.9948 against a between-class ceiling of 0.908). That turns glyph identification from fuzzy scoring into lookup and is reusable on every other Latin/digit table in this corpus. (2) The relikd token table is 6/11 on the disputed cells and scream314's token table is 11/11. Any other transcription in this repo sourced from relikd carries a measurable error rate; re-adjudicating those pages with pixelmatch.py is a small job with a validated instrument already behind it. entries.control_detail: Round 19 T2, control 10/10. Canon is correct on all 19 lines in count AND position; Round 8's diffs were its own dot extractor, which counted every sub-30px component as one dot when a '.' is a 24-60px lozenge fragmenting into up to 23 components. Coverage raised 170/604 -> 604/604.
entries.result: ALL 19 LINES READ. Canon is correct on every one, in count AND in position. The Round 8 diffs are its own instrument, in two distinct failure modes: 10/19 are a line-alignment slip (Round 8's dot count for the image row equals canon's separator count at a NEARBY canon line, d in -4..+4; its count-based DP aligned 599 of 604 lines where T2's mask-based map aligns 604/604), and 9/19 are a dot-extraction failure - four of them (glines 536, 538, 545, 550, all on dense pages 47-48) Round 8 measured at ZERO dots, where cropping gline 545 shows six separator dots plainly, exactly matching canon's six '-'. Root cause of the whole shortlist: Round 8 counted EVERY component with h < 30 as one separator dot, but the mark classes are cleanly bimodal - a word separator '-' is ONE dot spanning 9-10 px (2,767 of them) while a sentence mark '.' is a LOZENGE spanning 24-60 px that fragments into 3/4/10/13/23 components (187 of them). A single '.' therefore contributed up to 23 to Round 8's count. This independently confirms round18/L4's fitted advance widths ('.' 1.82 against '-' 0.32).
entries.coverage: All 19 shortlisted lines, and the whole-book audit behind them: 604/604 lines. Canon 2,764 '-' and 183 '.'; image 2,767 '-' and 187 '.'. Lines with exact separator counts 582/604 (96.36%); with exact separator POSITIONS 580/604 (96.03%).

entries.threshold: H1: a band decodes to an English word or known Cicada string of length >= 8 under a cipher validated on the solved pages (run confusable-tolerant, see control_detail). H2: identical short-band content recurring at >= 3 sites. H3/H4/H5: >= 3 exact matches (page index / prime index / one of 12 checksum forms), family-wise p < 1.67e-4, Bonferroni 8.3e-5 within H5. H6: >= 8-char English via a pointer reading, or doublet-landing p < 0.001. H7: p < 0.001 that band lengths are drawn from {2^k}, against a SIZE-MATCHED null. H8: p < 0.001 non-uniform position or a >= 8-char decode. Plus a quadgram-vs-null test per band: score must exceed its own size-matched null MAX over 2,000 draws from the LP2 rune frequency distribution.

FORCING: the author constrained the CIPHERTEXT so that a ciphertext-visible positional subset (line initials, page initials, word initials, or their finals) spells or encodes something. Detectable with no key at all. Motivated by round17/D-01, which proved the anti-repeat filter is machine-applied, i.e. the author demonstrably wrote a rejection sampler that enforces a ciphertext-level predicate; forcing is the hypothesis that the sampler enforced a second one.

entries.threshold: inherited hard gate p < 0.001 (campaign14/REDTEAM-PROPOSALS.md), Bonferroni-corrected over the 21 pre-registered tests to alpha_test = 4.762e-5
entries.control_detail: Synthetic 12,956-rune streams with LP2's exact separator pattern and page geometry, drawn from the fitted H0 generator (uniform runes under a memoryless lag-1 anti-repeat rejection filter at s=0.8075) and laid out by the SAME greedy line-breaker with the SAME fitted glyph widths, so the control carries the real book's inspection-paradox size bias rather than a straw null. Generator validated before use: doublet rate 0.006719 +/- 0.000614 vs LP2's 0.006638; IoC*N 0.99991 vs 1.000. Corroboration: the layout-aware null built on purely synthetic forcing-free streams has mean 64.68 sd 14.62, matching the null built by reflowing the real shuffled ciphertext (65.60, sd 14.48). A fraction f of the 594 line initials was then forced to a fixed 594-rune phrase under BOTH mechanisms (M1 assign-unconditionally; M2 filter-wins), 200 replicates per cell, 2,000 null streams for the critical values. MEASURED POWER at alpha_test=4.762e-5: the layout-corrected detector D_layout has false-positive rate 0.000/200 at f=0 and power 1.000 at f>=0.60 under both mechanisms (f80 = 0.60), collapsing to 0.595/0.460 at f=0.40 and 0.045/0.060 at f=0.30. Arm C's D_C1 reaches 0.765 at f=1.00 under M1 and 0.000 at EVERY f under M2. Arm B's planted-English acrostic control recovered at -4.372 against a bar of -6.806. CRITICAL NEGATIVE CONTROL RESULT: the detector C-02 literally specified -- the same chi-square judged against a FLAT null -- has a measured false-positive rate of 0.490 at f=0, i.e. it fires on forcing-free LP2-like data half the time, against a nominal 4.8e-5. Its power is also non-monotone (0.490 at f=0, ~0.30 at f=0.05-0.10). The literal C-02 detector is not usable on this object; only the layout-corrected one is, and the negative reported here is the layout-corrected one's.
entries.null: Arm A: exact multivariate-hypergeometric size-matched resampling of positions from the ciphertext's own urn (200,000 draws, resolution floor 5.0e-6), plus a layout-aware null that reflows shuffled text through the fitted greedy line-breaker. Arm B: max-statistic null over the identical 232-variant Gematria-Primus sweep applied to size-matched draws from the ciphertext, Gumbel-fitted to the pre-registered alpha. Arm C: allocation null over doublet counts preserving the measured anti-repeat suppression, plus a constrained permutation null for the difference channel.
entries.result: ONE pre-registered test fired and it is typographic, not cryptographic. A1 (line-initial runes, n=594): chi2(28)=78.656, empirical p<=5.0e-6, asymptotic p=1.06e-6 -- clears the gate by two orders of magnitude and exceeds all 200,000 flat-null draws (max 74.04). Post-hoc confound analysis identifies the cause as the inspection paradox under a greedy width-based line-breaker: the rune straddling the right margin is length-biased into the next line's first slot, so P(rune r begins a line) ~ p(r)*width(r). Rune widths recovered by least squares from the 539 width-limited lines correlate at +0.879 with BabelStone Runic advance widths (external, independent of the ciphertext); they correlate at +0.697 with the line-initial log excess; they drop the statistic to 38.73 (p~0.085) and, cross-validated on held-out lines, to 31.04 (p~0.32); and a reflow null built from them (53.5% exact line-length reproduction, 82.5% within +/-1 rune) has mean 65.60 vs the observed 78.66, giving p_layout=0.177. All other 20 pre-registered tests NEGATIVE, including page-initial (p=0.387), word-initial (p=0.706), all six Arm B message families (56,376 keyless Gematria-Primus reads; every family's observed maximum falls BELOW its own max-statistic null maximum, with the 594-rune line-initial sequence at -7.115 against a null max of -6.968 and a null mean of -7.199), and every Arm C position-conditioned filter statistic.
entries.coverage: 12,956 runes / 55 pages / 594 lines / 2,928 words / 219 sentence units, pages 0-54 only. Arm A: 10 positional subsets (line/word/page/sentence initials and finals plus two adjacency controls), chi-square vs both the full-text distribution and flat uniform, 200,000 exact size-matched draws each. Arm B: 6 families x 232 Gematria-Primus variants per read (forward/reverse x identity/Atbash x 29 Caesar shifts x keep/drop-F), covering the 594-rune line-initial sequence, 55 per-page acrostics, 108 per-page main and anti diagonals, 77 every-Nth-line-initial subsequences for N=2..12 at all phases, the 55-rune page-initial and page-final strings, and the 2,928-rune word-initial and word-final strings; max-statistic nulls with the identical sweep. Arm C: doublet residual rate and 29-bin difference channel conditioned on position-within-line and position-within-word, suppression estimates with Wilson intervals, and the mutual information between each line-final rune and the next line-initial rune. Durable by-products: a 29-rune glyph-width table recovered from the transcription and externally validated against a real runic font, and a validated greedy line-breaker model of the book's typesetting. Measured sensitivity floor: forcing of >=60% of the 594 line initials would have been detected with probability 1.000; below f~0.40 the corrected detector is largely blind and at f<=0.20 it is blind.
entries.not_covered: (1) Arm C is badly underpowered in the deficit direction: with only 539 line-boundary transitions at a ~0.7% residual rate it can detect a boundary suppression only at s <= -0.712 (a 71% EXCESS of boundary doublets) at the pre-registered alpha, and CANNOT detect a deficit at any alpha, not even a total ban on boundary doublets. A forcing scheme whose conflicts were resolved by re-rolling is therefore invisible to Arm C at this sample size. (2) Arm A's layout correction now sets the sensitivity floor for line-initial forcing: because typography already lifts the line-initial chi-square to a null mean of 65.6, weak forcing is masked -- see the measured f80 in RESULTS.md section 5 for the exact fraction of lines that would have to be forced. (3) Not tested: forcing on subsets this lane did not enumerate (column-wise readings across pages, ornament-relative positions, per-page rune-index arithmetic, positions defined by the 47 catalogued ornament bands -- that is lane L3's ground); forcing of a NON-rune-valued feature (word lengths, line lengths, punctuation placement) rather than of rune identity; and forcing detectable only jointly with a key hypothesis. (4) Arm B scored English only; a forced acrostic in a non-English language, in digits, or in prime values would not have been seen by the quadgram scorer -- this is the same English-only scorer limitation lane L7 is auditing. (5) The whole lane rests on the krisyotam transcription's LINE BREAKS being the book's real line breaks; a from-scratch re-read (PARKED.md, per-rune vision) would independently confirm both the geometry and the glyph-width table.
entries.reproduce: cd liber-primus/analysis/round18/L4-forcing && python3 parse_structure.py && python3 armA_uniformity.py 200000 && python3 confound_layout.py 5000 && python3 armC_rejection.py 200000 && python3 armB_message.py 1000 && python3 control_power.py
entries.reopens_if: (a) a re-transcription changes the line breaks or the 86/4 doublet counts, since the whole layout correction is conditioned on them; (b) anyone measures real glyph widths from the 400-DPI page renders and they disagree with the fitted table (corr +0.879 with BabelStone is supportive, not decisive -- the book's own font was not identified); (c) a scorer that is not English-only, or a non-rune-valued feature channel (word lengths, line lengths, punctuation), is applied to the same positional subsets; (d) lane L3's ornament catalogue yields positional subsets this lane did not enumerate; (e) sample size at line boundaries can be raised -- e.g. by pooling LP1's runic pages -- which is the only way to lift Arm C out of its deficit-direction blind spot.
entries.notes: Two instrument findings are worth more than the verdict. FIRST: a flat null is WRONG for any line-position statistic on LP2. Typography alone lifts the line-initial chi-square from a flat-null mean of 26.9 to 65.6, so a flat null manufactures p ~ 1e-6 out of a greedy line-breaker. Any future acrostic or positional attack must use the layout-aware null in confound_layout.py. SECOND, and recorded per Round 18 rule 2: this lane's own first draft of Arm C used a permutation null that reshuffled line-initial runes among themselves, which destroys the anti-repeat filter -- a property established at >=0.99 power by round17/D-01 and therefore part of H0, not something to randomise away. The tell was C1 returning p = 1.00000 and C4 returning a null mean of 83.7 against 27 df. Both were rebuilt (allocation null preserving the measured suppression; difference channel restricted to bins 1-28) before any verdict was taken. A null that destroys a known H0 property cannot test anything -- it only measures how strongly H0 holds.

entries.hypothesis: Higher-order model test against matched controls. The proposal asked for cross-validated bits/rune at PPM orders 1-8 vs 1,000 controls generated with campaign11's suppression model. What was actually run (`recon/i6_mdl/mdl_test.py`) uses 40 uniform-random controls and context order ≤5, with no cross-validation — so the one anomaly it found (order-1 entropy dip, z=−14.6) is exactly what an unmatched control makes inevitable.

Homophonic-downward (surjective 29→k, k=5..26) annealing/EM search. Closed only by an inference from bigram flatness (Campaign XIV P4, +0.81σ); the search the proposal specified — anneal the partition, validate on synthetic homophonic ciphertext, score against a 1,000-shuffle envelope, check generalisation to held-out pages — was never coded.
Non-additive ciphertext-feedback coefficient sweep ran on 3 of 55 pages (p0/p5/p20) at orders k≤3 with 3 seeds, then was written up as "closes the last additive-adjacent corner".

Payload as an RSA signature/ciphertext under known Cicada moduli: compute pow(s,e,n) in both endiannesses for every published 3301 modulus and pattern-match PKCS#1 v1.5 / PSS structure. Zero-false-positive test, minutes of compute.
entries.threshold: PREREG B.1/B.5: HIT iff a STRUCTURAL match - not a score, so there is no threshold to tune. PKCS#1 v1.5 signature: leading 00 01, >= 8 FF bytes, 00, then a DigestInfo DER prefix from round16's OID table (the 'strict' tier); padding-frame-only counts as 'loose' and does not qualify as a hit. EMSA-PSS: 0xBC trailer, MGF1-unmasked DB of the form 00*k || 01 || salt with k >= 8 ('strict'). Anything else is a null.

control_detail.positive: Locally generated RSA-2048 key, genuine signatures from the `cryptography` library. PKCS#1 v1.5 signature: matcher FIRES at the strict tier (202 FF bytes, then a real SHA-256 DigestInfo). EMSA-PSS (MGF1-SHA-256, salt 32): matcher FIRES at the strict tier (190 zero bytes, then 0x01, saltlen 32). PKCS#1 v1.5 type 2 encryption block: matcher FIRES (loose tier; type-2 blocks carry no DigestInfo, so no strict tier exists for them).
control_detail.negative: 10,000 random 256-byte blocks: PKCS#1 v1.5 signature 0 strict / 0 loose; PKCS#1 v1.5 type 2 0 loose; EMSA-PSS 0 strict / 1 loose. The single loose PSS false positive (measured rate 1e-4) is exactly why the strict tier requires >= 8 zero bytes before the 0x01 delimiter; the strict tier fired zero times on noise.
control_detail.key_verification: Both 4096-bit moduli identified by computing the RFC 4880 12.2 v4 fingerprint from the OpenPGP packet bytes, not from filenames, and independently confirmed with `gpg --with-colons --import-options show-only --import`. Primary 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F (key id 181F01E57A35090F), subkey DEC57731ACCBFD11EEBA13434D390ECF671DDEB1, both RSA-4096 e=65537, uid 'Cicada 3301 (845145127)', created 1325734783 = 2012-01-05.

entries.null: H0 was no structure. Not rejected: 162/162 tuples produced no structural match while the matchers demonstrably fire on genuine signatures.
entries.result: NEGATIVE (structural null, with the named Round 16 coverage gap closed). Round 16 recorded E-01 as coverage-limited because 'the 7A35090F RSA-4096 moduli (the correct size) were not on disk and not fetched'. Re-running round16/zeroFP/zerofp_tests.py shows what that actually amounted to: 1 modulus, 8 pow() checks, ALL EIGHT SKIPPED for s>=n - Round 16 evaluated ZERO modular exponentiations for E-01. The moduli were on disk all along, under ten witnesses including two keyserver pulls, and no network fetch was needed. Round 16's stated justification for not fetching them - 'under a 4096-bit modulus, pow(s,e,n) would trivially return s^e as-is (s << n), so PKCS1 padding is impossible' - is arithmetically false for every e > 1 (s is 2048-bit; s^3 is ~6144-bit and s^65537 is ~1.3e8 bits, both of which reduce mod a 4096-bit n). C1 ran the test: for the 3301 moduli, 54 (modulus x endianness x block alignment x exponent x payload variant) tuples evaluated and 36 arithmetically excluded because s >= n, ZERO structural matches. Broadened to every RSA public key on disk (22 distinct keys from 3,716 key-shaped files), 594 tuples evaluated, 144 excluded, ZERO structural matches. One arithmetic exclusion is itself informative: the payload's leading byte 0xcb exceeds the leading bytes of both 3301 moduli (0xc1 primary, 0xbc subkey), so the 256-byte payload placed in the HIGH half of a 4096-bit block is already too large to be a valid signature representative under either key - that placement is excluded by arithmetic, not merely untested. Independently replicated in the same wall-clock window by the concurrent round18/L5-payload run (different matcher implementation, different encoding enumeration, same verdict NULL and same skip pattern). || SUB-RESULT B (Crypt::RSA::ES::OAEP, the authors own declared scheme, never tested by anyone before): NULL. R1 found 3301 naming the library in signed text and C3s PGP-VERIFICATION-TABLE.json confirms both carrier messages PASS under 181F01E57A35090F (this-message-will-only-be-displayed.asc 2012-01-15T01:39:42Z; 2014-01-rsa-oaep-challenge.asc = welcome.asc, same sha256 c9053eb4..., 2014-01-06T07:35:27Z), both carrying Version: 1.99 / Scheme: Crypt::RSA::ES::OAEP. 126 rows, 36 arithmetically excluded, ZERO hits, over three sub-tests: the payload read directly as an ES::OAEP encoded block (36 configurations), pow(s,e,n) read as an encoded block at emLen in {k-1,k}, and block-count arithmetic. KEY-SIZE COVERAGE, stated plainly: Crypt::RSA concatenates k-byte blocks, so a 256-byte payload is a whole ciphertext only when k divides 256 -- i.e. under a 512-bit (4 blocks), 1024-bit (2 blocks) or 2048-bit (1 block) key. 3301 published NO key of any of those sizes. The two 4096-bit moduli give k=512 and the 2013 key k=54; neither divides 256, so all three published moduli are excluded structurally, not merely untested. Two artifact findings: the Convert::ASCII::Armour container is len(name)NUL len(value)NUL name value with NO separator (the comma that looks like a delimiter is 0x2c, the ciphertexts own first byte; reading it as a delimiter makes the value one byte short of its declared length, and the armours MD5 matches the compressed blob exactly, so nothing was lost in transmission); and the recovered 39-byte message body is not ASCII and lacks the 0x01 delimiter PKCS#1 v2.1 predicts, recorded as an open observation rather than a claim.
entries.coverage: Moduli: 3301's 7A35090F primary (4096-bit, e=65537, fingerprint 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F) and its subkey (4096-bit, DEC57731ACCBFD11EEBA13434D390ECF671DDEB1), both fingerprinted from the OpenPGP packet body rather than from a filename, plus the 432-bit 2013 puzzle modulus, plus 20 further RSA public keys found by scanning all 3,716 key-shaped files under corpus/ and liber-primus/ (none of them 3301's; they are Round 18 L8's base-rate keys - Tor Browser devs, Tails, GnuPG release, bitcoin-core - and two solver-tool keys). Payload variants: canon_256.bin, canon_256_decpref.bin, payload_resolved.bin. Encodings: big-endian, little-endian (byte-reversed), and for moduli wider than the payload both left-aligned (zero-padded low) and right-aligned (zero-padded high) block placements. Exponents: 65537, 3, 17. Matchers: PKCS#1 v1.5 type 1 with DigestInfo for MD5/SHA-1/224/256/384/512, PKCS#1 v1.5 type 2, EMSA-PSS under MGF1-SHA-1/256/384/512 at salt lengths {0,20,28,32,48,64,hLen}. 738 tuples enumerated in total. SUB-RESULT B additionally covers: Crypt::RSA::ES::OAEP 1.99 at emLen in {k-1, k}, MGF1-SHA-1, label P empty, against all three published moduli and all three payload variants in both endiannesses, plus the payload read directly as an encoded block at block sizes {256,128,64} and offsets {0,1}.
entries.not_covered: (a) RSA moduli 3301 never published - in particular the moduli behind the three 2014 onion RSA blobs, which are encrypted MESSAGES (ciphertexts), not public keys, so their n is not recoverable from what is on disk. (b) The 432-bit 2013 modulus as a signing key over a 54-byte WINDOW of the payload rather than the whole 256 bytes - all 18 of its tuples are excluded by s >= n and no windowing was pre-registered. (c) Blinded signatures, partially-known signatures, and any signature of which the payload is a fragment. (d) OAEP and raw unpadded RSA. (e) Any payload transform outside the four enumerated integer encodings (e.g. bit-reversed, hex-ASCII, or a re-ordered byte permutation). (f) e outside {65537, 3, 17}. (g) 512-, 1024- and 2048-bit RSA keys -- the ONLY sizes under which the 256-byte payload is a whole number of Crypt::RSA blocks; 3301 published none, so this is uncovered because the modulus does not exist in the record, not because it was skipped. (h) OAEP with a non-empty label P. (i) Crypt::RSA::SS::PSS and Crypt::RSA::ES::PKCS1v15 as SIGNATURE schemes -- only ES::OAEP could be measured from a held artifact.

Anyone verifying a 3301 key by filename would draw the wrong conclusion, and short-id collisions are a known attack on exactly this habit. e01_extended.py deliberately EXTENDS round16's instrument (importing zerofp_tests.pkcs1_v15_check and zerofp_tests.check_digest_info unchanged) rather than replacing it, so a hit here would have been a hit there. | supersedes: Round 16's partially-run / coverage-limited E-01, whose stated blocker was 'the 7A35090F RSA-4096 moduli were not on disk and not fetched'.

entries.hypothesis: Payload as meta-parameters: (a) slide a 56-byte window and test for a permutation of 0-55 (chance ≈1e-24 per window); (b) read the payload as 85-128 gap values (8/16-bit LE/BE, varint) and rank-correlate against the real doublet gaps [122, 85, 249, 197, 129, …]. Both "instant"; neither run. Round 8 POINTERS correlated the gaps against primes and Fibonacci, never against the payload.
entries.threshold: E-02A: a 56-byte window of the payload IS a permutation of 0..55 (exact, no scoring). E-02B: |rank correlation| > 0.5 on the doublet-gap sequence, a bar chosen because p(|r|>0.5) < 1e-5 at this length.
entries.control_detail: Shared zeroFP lane control, pre-registered in zeroFP/PREREG.md: `python tests/validate.py` must print ALL VALIDATIONS PASSED before any result is trusted, and it did (recorded in zeroFP/RESULTS.md). These are EXACT tests rather than scored searches -- their false-positive rate is analytic, not estimated -- so the control that matters is the trust anchor plus the pre-registered bar, both satisfied.
entries.result: NULL (complete) -- verdict NULL. E-02A: all 201 consecutive 56-byte windows of the 256-byte payload checked, zero are a permutation of 0..55; 57-byte windows likewise zero. False-positive rate ~1e-24 per window, so this is a clean null with analytic certainty rather than a scored miss. E-02B: the 85 inter-doublet gaps carry no rank correlation above the bar.

entries.threshold: Pre-registered in round18/L1-toolchain/PREREG.md before any run. (a) EXACT IJG QUALITY asserted only if interval-arithmetic inversion over libjpeg's temp=(base*scale+50)/100 rule admits exactly one integer quality consistent with all 64 luma AND all 64 chroma coefficients, and PC1 recovers 6/6 planted qualities. (b) ENCODER NAMED only if a control pipeline reproduces byte-identical DQT tables + identical Huffman-table classification + identical subsampling + identical component-count behaviour; anything less is written as 'consistent with'. (c) YEAR BOUND asserted only from a dated artefact inside the file, quoted verbatim. (d) FONT IDENTIFIED only if best candidate's mean per-glyph distance falls inside the PC3 degraded-self-match band AND beats the runner-up by >=2 sigma over >=20 rune classes.

PC2b (chain reproduction): `gs -sDEVICE=jpeg -dJPEGQ=92 -r400` followed by ImageMagick at quality 92 reproduces the LP2 vector with BYTE-IDENTICAL DQT tables (luma sha1 c96e442f9ce9a1965c6084df936558fcc335a69f, chroma sha1 cd6e3767d9c4da25c4f8126038b332d0ac48f244), identical marker order for both the colour and the grayscale class, and identical JFIF block. Glyph extraction uses the VALIDATED R9 template-DP reader (96.93% agreement over 5,207 compared glyphs, analysis/retranscribe/diff_report.json), explicitly NOT round12/frontB/forceseg.py which fails its control at 12.9%.

result.ghostscript_bound: TWO-SIDED, BYTE-EXACT. The LP2 profile's PCS-illuminant bytes (offset 68..79) are 0000f6d5 00010000 0000d32c, md5 e409cef13cd06f6b371f6cddc8e31fcf. Measured against ghostpdl tags: 9.00/9.01/9.02 ship a 3144-byte profile with the canonical illuminant (no match); 9.04, 9.05, 9.06, 9.07, 9.09, 9.10, 9.12, 9.14, 9.15, 9.16, 9.17, 9.18, 9.19, 9.20, 9.21 all ship a 2576-byte profile BYTE-IDENTICAL to the LP2 one; 9.22, 9.26, 9.50, 9.53.3 and 10.06.0 ship the corrected profile (md5 27d2435a749ae91e9974bf7a109a03e5). Artifex introduced the matching profile at 9.04 (2011-08-05) and corrected the two illuminant bytes at 9.22 (2017-10-04). BOUND: Ghostscript >= 9.04 and <= 9.21. Intersected with the artifact's own publication date (onion7, May 2014) the operative window is 9.04-9.14, i.e. 2011-08 to 2014-03. Ubuntu 12.04 LTS shipped Ghostscript 9.05 (2012-02), inside the window and the same distro generation that ships the GnuPG 1.4.11 the author signed with for three years. This also rules out the pages having been re-rendered with any post-2017 Ghostscript.

entries.hypothesis: corpus/GAPS.md G-02 (★★★★★): the signed message texts are quoted in research/03-*.md and .asc files are held, but no file in this repository records which signatures verify against key 7A35090F and which do not — despite that being the repo's own declared authenticity test (KNOWLEDGE.json: authenticity_test). Build the table: every claimed Cicada message as an .asc, gpg --verify against the canonical key, PASS/FAIL/NO-SIG with the signature timestamp.
entries.threshold: PASS iff gpg emits GOODSIG+VALIDSIG for fingerprint 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F. FAIL = a signature packet is present and it does not. NO-SIG = no signature block. A FAIL counts as a finding about the MESSAGE only if the same normalised signed body has no PASSing copy elsewhere in the corpus; otherwise it is a transport defect. Fixed in PREREG.md before the run.
entries.control_detail: Four controls, all met. C1: an untouched known-good file yields GOODSIG 181F01E57A35090F. C2: flipping ONE character of the signed body yields BADSIG and no GOODSIG. C3: a message clear-signed by a freshly generated foreign RSA-2048 key yields NO_PUBKEY for that keyid and no GOODSIG for 3301. C4: the signature-packet timestamp is still recovered from the C2-tampered file unchanged (1325738763 -> 1325738763). Keyring isolation is enforced in code: the script builds a throwaway GNUPGHOME each run and aborts if it holds any primary key other than the canonical one.
entries.null: H1 (every canon message verifies; no second signing key appears) is refuted if a message with no clean copy anywhere fails, or if a second signing key ID appears.
entries.result: H1 NOT refuted. 228 .asc files scanned repo-wide: 192 PASS, 3 FAIL, 22 NO-SIG, 11 KEY. Deduplicated to distinct signed texts: 54 messages, 54 verify, 0 do not. Exactly ONE signing key ID appears across every signed message in the tree — 181F01E57A35090F; no second key anywhere, in any mirror, in any era. 54 distinct verified signature timestamps spanning 2012-01-05T03:46:03Z to 2017-04-04T23:23:28Z. The 3 FAILs are one message (2013-01-03 'Welcome again.') mirrored three times, all failing with gpg's own diagnosis `invalid armor header: Welcome again.` — the mirror dropped the blank line after the `Hash: SHA1` armor header, so the first body line is parsed as a header; 4 other copies of the identical normalised body PASS, and the repo's repaired copy (1538 B vs 1536 B) PASSes carrying the identical signature packet. Transport defect, not a canon failure. INCIDENTAL FINDINGS: (1) 19 files in liber-primus/analysis/round10/L6-archives/fetched/jaxonkuipers/comms/ are 199-byte HTTP `429: Too Many Requests` pages, not communications — same failure mode as the _560.00 truncation in G-12, still in the tree and still glob-reachable. (2) The digest algorithm is SHA-1 on 53 of 54 messages and SHA-512 on the last (2017-04-04) — the signing toolchain changed exactly once, between 2016-01-01 and 2017-04-04. (3) corpus/A-primary-artifacts/ibotpeaches/keys/67F363C61BA8FB6FDBA9C47D0670B0E57A35090F.asc is named for a fingerprint that is NOT the canonical one (they share only the trailing 32-bit short ID); the key inside IS canonical, so it is a mislabel — but it is a live argument for never verifying by short ID.
entries.coverage: Every *.asc file in the repository as of 2026-08-26: 228 files, 113 distinct by sha256, 54 distinct signed message bodies. Verified under GnuPG 2.4.8 against an isolated keyring holding only 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F. Both a human-readable table and a full machine record were written.
entries.not_covered: (a) COMPLETENESS OF THE CORPUS. This verifies the .asc files this repo holds; it cannot verify a message nobody mirrored. Every holding is a mirror-of-a-mirror and corpus/GAPS.md G-12 applies to all of it. (b) The 2023 public self-claim: no .asc attributable to it is held here, so this run neither confirms nor refutes it. (c) WALL-CLOCK TRUTH of any timestamp — RFC 4880 creation time is a hashed subpacket from the signer's own clock and is settable by the signer; AUDITOR-LOOP-2026-07-28 already refuted the timezone biometric built on these, and that refutation stands. (d) AUTHORSHIP — a good signature proves keyholder continuity and nothing more. (e) Signatures on non-.asc carriers (inline .txt, .sig detached files) were not enumerated separately. (f) Whether the 19 stub files have clean upstream equivalents beyond those already refetched into corpus/A-primary-artifacts/pgp/messages/.

entries.hypothesis: REFRAMED to something falsifiable. The register's question ('who is mruzuki') is not testable from public sources and is out of scope. The testable question: was the `mruzuki` / `cicadeur` key (02BD208AFB8AFF75, mruzuki@gmail.com, created 2012-01-12, self-revoked 2012-01-22) produced by the SAME OpenPGP toolchain as 3301's 7A35090F? Same-toolchain is a real, checkable technical claim; a name is not.
entries.threshold: Fixed in PREREG.md before retrieval. MATCH = identical ordered preference lists AND identical self-sig hash algorithm AND identical key-flag/feature bytes. MISMATCH = any ordered preference list differs. INDECISIVE = the preferences agree but are the era default of a common client, so the agreement carries no discriminating information. Declared in advance: a MATCH would be weak evidence at best and would NOT be reported as a link to a person.
entries.control_detail: The instrument (gpg --list-packets on keyserver exports) is the same reader validated in the G-02 run, where controls C1-C4 all passed. The DISCRIMINATION control — a base rate for the preference triplet among 2012-era keys — was attempted and is reported as UNDER-POWERED: only 4 public project release keys were retrievable (Tor Browser Developers, Bitcoin Core, GnuPG release, Tails), none created in Jan 2012 (2010/2014/2014/2015), and a live key's UID self-signature is REISSUED on every edit so a keyserver copy shows the preferences of the last edit rather than of creation — which is why the 2010-created key in the sample carries the modern GnuPG 2.1+ list. That sample was NOT used to decide the verdict. The verdict rests instead on GnuPG's own released source: gnupg-1.4.16 g10/keygen.c, keygen_set_std_prefs(), whose compiled-in default with no gpg.conf override is exactly S9 S8 S7 S3 S2 / H8 H2 H9 H10 H11 / Z2 Z3 Z1 with mdc=1 and modify=0 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gpg/gnupg/gnupg-1.4.16/g10/keygen.c, retrieved 2026-08-26).
entries.null: H3 (same toolchain) is supported only if the shared fields carry discriminating information. If the shared values are the software's own factory default, the comparison is INDECISIVE by construction.
entries.result: INDECISIVE - round18's verdict stands, and C3 confirms it is not disturbed by the new L1 cross-check. Where the SOFTWARE chose, the two keys agree; where a HUMAN chose, they differ: key size 4096 vs 2048, expiry policy none vs ONE DAY, revocation never vs 2012-01-22 (reason 0x03 'no longer used'). The matching preference lists S9 S8 S7 S3 S2 / H8 H2 H9 H10 H11 / Z2 Z3 Z1, features 01, keyserver-prefs 80 are EXACTLY GnuPG 1.4.x/2.0.x keygen_set_std_prefs() defaults, which in January 2012 describes most new OpenPGP keys on Earth.
entries.coverage: Every field of both keys' self-signature packets compared: version, pubkey algo, key size, creation, self-sig digest algo, key flags, expiry, all three ordered preference lists, features, keyserver prefs, revocation state and reason.
entries.not_covered: Any non-packet link. Breach-DB and people-search lookups on the key's email address were DECLINED IN ADVANCE and not run - a scope decision, not an untried lead. Resolving a private individual's identity from a puzzle handle is not a cryptanalytic result and would carry no cryptographic proof of key control.
entries.reopens_if: A message signed by 02BD208AFB8AFF75 is recovered (that would make the relationship testable rather than circumstantial); an archived public post ties the handle to any Cicada-specific fact before its disclosure date; a 2012-frozen key population becomes available so the preference base rate can actually be measured; or a keyserver upload-time record surfaces.
entries.notes: The connection to Cicada 3301 remains SPECULATED and this lane does not upgrade it: it rests on a handle containing 'cicadeur' and on temporal adjacency. There is no signature, no key-material relationship, no web-of-trust path, and — per the verdict — no toolchain discriminator. What the key does show is the same designed-anonymity profile the 2026-07-28 auditor identified as the strongest supportable conclusion in this case: self-expiring, WoT-isolated, deliberately short-lived key material.

Never executed as a search. A dated, archive-attested post referencing a Cicada-specific element BEFORE its public disclosure date would be the strongest external evidence in the whole case.
entries.threshold: Fixed in PREREG.md before searching. HIT = a dated, archive-attested post before its element's disclosure date, with a URL and a capture that carries the date. NEGATIVE = every named archive searched with every named term over the stated window, no hit — reported as a BOUND ('searched X, terms Y, window Z, nothing'), never as a clearance. A hit whose date cannot be independently established from the archive is NOT a hit. Anti-motivated-reasoning clause: 'someone mentioned cicadas' is not a hit; 'someone discussed runic ciphers' is not a hit.
entries.positive_control: PARTIAL. The metzdowd half is searched against the REAL corpus (monthly mbox files downloaded and zgrep'd locally), so its silence is a measurable bound. The bitcointalk half rests on a search index rather than a local corpus and is therefore labelled 'reported', not 'verified' — that half has no control and its negative is correspondingly weaker.
entries.control_detail: Term set and window were fixed in PREREG.md before any retrieval. The grep is demonstrably sensitive: it DOES fire on the post-disclosure material (19 'cicada' hits, plus '845145127', 'instar', 'highly intelligent individuals', 'mabinogion', 'outguess', 'gematria', 'anglo-saxon rune'), all of them inside metzdowd 2013-November — so a term-set or encoding failure is excluded. A search that finds the post-disclosure signal and not the pre-disclosure one is a real negative over the corpus it covers.
entries.null: H4 (a pre-2012-01-04 archived post references a Cicada-specific element) is supported only by a dated, archive-attested capture. Absence over a searchable corpus is a bound on that corpus, not a clearance.
entries.result: FOUND-ERROR in the previous run, then a much weaker bound than round18 appeared to report. Round 18's predisclosure_search.sh hit a fixed pipermail URL for every month of 2011-2013 and treated a non-200 as 'searched, nothing'. Its own fetch log shows metzdowd returned 404 for 28 of 36 months and cypherpunks returned http=000 for ALL 36. http=000 is a transport failure, not a 404, and neither is a searched month. C3 re-probed both. metzdowd: the index lists 274 monthly archives and for 2011-2013 exactly EIGHT exist (2011-August, then nothing until 2013-June) - the list was dormant - so of the 13 months in the hard window 2011-01-01 -> 2012-01-04 the archive holds ONE. cypherpunks: two independent faults, neither of them absence - the host's TLS certificate has EXPIRED (so a verifying client fails before seeing an HTTP status) AND the list no longer runs pipermail at all (/pipermail/cypherpunks/ returns 404; the archive is served by HyperKitty at /archives/list/cypherpunks@lists.cpunks.org/). Round 18 was pointed at a dead endpoint behind a broken certificate and recorded the result as a negative.
entries.coverage: MAILING-LIST ARM: metzdowd cryptography 1 of 13 months of the hard window (2011-August only), 8 months / 1.9 MB downloaded and grepped for all 12 terms. cypherpunks @ cpunks.org 0 of 13 months - the archive holds ZERO messages before 2013; 2013 fetched in full (5.5 MB, 2645 messages) and grepped. mail-archive.com cypherpunks: search interface only, no mbox export, yields no coverage number.

Round 17 established the anti-repeat filter is machine-applied, so the program that produced the pad also typeset the book -- and typesetting decisions (line fill, margins, where a line breaks) are a place a designer can put data without touching the ciphertext.
entries.threshold: Each of 11 channels tested three ways. (a) two-state screen: PASS iff GMM component separation >= 2.0 sigma AND dBIC > 10 for two components. (b) bit decode: median-threshold -> 8 packings (fwd/rev x 5-bit/8-bit) x 8 phases -> English 4-gram score; PASS iff p < 0.001 against a 2,000-draw size-matched shuffle null. (c) correlation: Spearman rho against per-line rune statistics, PASS iff p < 0.001 Bonferroni-corrected over the channel x statistic grid (3.7e-5).

control_detail.C-3b decoder validation: Real ASCII planted noise-free in the bit channel is recovered by the same detector at p = 0.0005. PASS -- so the eight bit-decode nulls are silence from a working instrument, not from a dead one.
control_detail.C-3a power ceiling: Planting a 64-bit message in fill_ratio at k x the channel's own measured sd: the GMM screen sees a planted two-state channel from about 3 sd upward (2.26 sigma at 3 sd, 4.15 at 4 sd, 7.29 at 8 sd). Median-threshold bit recovery saturates at 0.859 because ASCII is not bit-balanced and a median threshold mis-assigns the minority bit -- a property of the pre-registered detector, reported rather than patched.

entries.null: 2,000-draw within-channel shuffle null for the bit decode; Bonferroni over the 24-test correlation grid; GMM BIC for the two-state screen.
entries.result: NEGATIVE with a stated power ceiling. Bimodality is REAL and survives its confound - row_height separates at 4.71 sigma overall and 7.90 sigma with last-lines and short pages removed, body_per_line at 3.93 sigma - so the book genuinely has two row-height states. It is NOT decodable: all 8 bit-decode channels score 0 against null means of 0.0-0.1, p=1.0000. Exactly 1 of 24 correlations clears Bonferroni (runes_per_line ~ mean_rune_idx, rho=-0.257, p=1.47e-10) and it is fully explained by typesetting: runes_per_line ~ mean GLYPH WIDTH is rho=-0.653 (p=8.3e-75) and the PARTIAL correlation controlling for width is rho=-0.018 (p=0.661). Wider runes, fewer runes per justified line. A typesetter, not a channel. H9: 1504 of 18514 components (8.12%) exceed 4 MAD-sigma and survive the stroke-and-height-matched re-test - far too dense to be a message and with no clause in the addendum covering it, so the discriminating question (registered before running) was whether flagging is predicted by render geometry: pooled AUC 0.709 (height), 0.707 (stroke width), 0.687 (area) against bars of >=0.80 render-artifact / <=0.60 unexplained -> PARTIALLY EXPLAINED, number reported, no claim made. H9 is now MEASURABLE for the first time; it is not a demonstrated channel.
entries.coverage: 616/616 text rows, 11 geometric channels, 8 bit packings, 24 correlations, 7 planted separations. 18514/18514 components for H9 over all 56 renders, plus 5 planted control levels.
entries.not_covered: Non-binary encodings of the row-height bimodality. Colour/chroma. Whether the page-15 anomaly is in the document rather than in this JPEG. Inter-word separator SHAPE (only counts and gaps were measured).

entries.notes: The first ink-tone detector (mean grey against a mean/sd reference) FAILED its own plant-and-recover control at recall 0.05-0.10, because a handful of genuinely lighter glyphs inflate the very dispersion they are tested against. The failure is recorded rather than hidden: it is exactly the failure mode this repository's discipline exists to catch, and the published result uses the repaired detector plus a near-confound-free statistic (component MINIMUM grey, which is insensitive to stroke width because a solid-black glyph reaches ~0 no matter how thin its strokes are).

entries.hypothesis: The anti-repeat rule is enforced on the CIPHERTEXT, not on the keystream and not on the plaintext. Seven loci were formalised and simulated: no filter (M0), ciphertext key-skip (M1, the repo's pinned model), ciphertext value-rewrite with the key staying aligned (M2), ciphertext deterministic nudge (M2n), keystream-filtered at generation (M3), plaintext-filtered before encipherment (M4), hard ciphertext rule (M5).
entries.threshold: A model may be called EXCLUDED only if the pairwise Gaussian log-LR classifier over 5 pre-registered primary statistics has power >= 0.99 to separate it from M1 at a 5% false-positive rate AND the real stream lies >= 4 sd outside that model's 200-replicate distribution on at least one primary statistic. Delta-spectrum nudge bar: Bonferroni over 28 cells, alpha=0.01 two-sided, |z| >= 3.57.
entries.control_detail: Fairness device: every parameterised model bisected to the REAL lag-1 rate (0.00663836) so the doublet rate carries no discriminating information, exactly as round17/P4 did. Instrument gate: the analytic filter constant s* = 0.81288 derived from r(s)=q(1-s)/(1-q*s) reproduces lane P4's independently bisected supp = 0.8131 to 2.2e-4. Classifier power measured at 1.000 on 5 of the 6 pairs.
entries.coverage: 200 replicates per model at n = 12,956 over an archaic-English (KJV) plaintext in runes; 5 primary statistics (lag1_rate, delta_chi2_df, max_abs_delta_z, bleed28_z, abab_z); a new Delta-spectrum statistic that concentrates a single-cell rewrite signature into 28 cells instead of P4's 783-cell off-diagonal bigram table. Keystream-side and plaintext-side filtering cannot reach the observed 0.664% doublet rate at ANY suppression strength - bisection drove both to supp=0.999 and both remain 17 sd above the real rate - because a uniform other stream washes the constraint out.
not_covered: M1 (ciphertext key-skip, key desynchronises) vs M2 (ciphertext value-rewrite, key stays aligned) are ciphertext-identical by construction; measured separation power 0.175, i.e. NOT-SEPARABLE. Any sweep must cover both mechanisms because they imply different decoders.
composite loci (e.g. a filter applied to the ciphertext of an already-deduplicated plaintext)

entries.notes: Settles the round10b/B4-G3 vs RECON-B/B-16 argument in B-16's favour: because the filter acts on the emitted symbol, the residual doublet rate is a property of the FILTER alone, independent of key and plaintext, so no doublet-based statistic discriminates key type in either direction.

entries.hypothesis: Rejection consumes keystream draws, so the keystream index is not the rune index. Quantify the drift, and determine which measured results in this repository depend on the alignment they assumed.

entries.control_detail: Analytic E[extra draws] = rho*(n-1) = 373.6 +/- 19.6 with rho = q*s/(1-q*s); 200 simulated enciphers of 12,956 English runes under skipdecode.encipher_keyskip at supp=0.8129 gave 374.5 +/- 21.1, 95% CI [328, 413]. Analytic inside CI.
entries.coverage: Closed form P(a rigid window of length L is drift-free) = (1-rho)^L, verified by 200 plant-and-recover trials per length at L in {25,50,100,120,200,400} with the CORRECT key and offset. Derives round17's previously unexplained prefilter survival constant: (1-rho)^PREFILTER_LEN = (1-rho)^24 = 0.495, which is pad-independent - exactly the pad-independence R17 measured (0.4-0.55 across seven pads of 4 MB to 118 MB) and attributed to 'pad statistics at least as much as size'. Closes round17 follow-up 3.
not_covered: the closed form is a LOWER bound on prefilter retention: a skip in the last one or two positions of a 24-rune window is often still survivable, which is why R17's measured mean 0.589 +/- 0.039 sits above 0.495
drift under the M2 value-rewrite locus is zero by construction; this entry quantifies drift only for the M1 key-skip locus, and A-LOCUS shows the ciphertext cannot say which is in force

entries.notes: The positive control is the finding. It is a measured demonstration that a genuinely correct key is undetectable at the offset every per-page test in this repository has used. The best score in the newly covered region (-6.0117) sits 0.17 above the expected null maximum for 1.37M trials, i.e. it is the order statistic, and it is BELOW the previously published best - so the draw-count correction opens a real region but does not move any existing best score. Incidental coverage correction for R16-KDF: three of its published top-50 secrets (1d00, 1d000000, 1d00000000000000) produce byte-identical keystreams, because in PBKDF2-HMAC the password IS the HMAC key and HMAC zero-pads a short key to the 64-byte block, so trailing zero bytes in a PBKDF2 password cannot change the output. Any seed dictionary that serialises integers at several byte widths has fewer distinct members than it counts; deduplicate on secret.rstrip(b'\x00') before quoting a coverage number. This does not affect R16-KDF's negative.

The two nulls agree at z = 0.32, which is an independent decoder-level confirmation of the cipher model on the real stream.

entries.hypothesis: Each accepted position certifies that the rejection sampler did not have to re-roll there, so 12,956 acceptance events are unspent constraints on the joint (plaintext, keystream). If the constraint system is anywhere near determined, a constraint-propagation / SAT / belief-propagation solver over the joint variables with an English plaintext prior should be built.
entries.threshold: Determined iff H(P) + H(K) - H(C) <= 0. Build the solver only if the deficit is <= 0 or within ~10^3 bits of zero under a stated extra assumption. Fixed in PREREG section 4 before the accounting was run.
entries.control_detail: C-PC: the same accounting applied to a 64-bit-seed derived keystream returns DETERMINED (deficit -29,283 bits), which agrees with round12/D3's demonstrated practical recovery of a planted short seed (beam -4.170, 98.9% character recovery). An accounting that called a demonstrably recoverable case under-determined would be wrong. Separately, the exact result was verified numerically: 1,000 enciphers each of a constant plaintext and an English plaintext give ciphertext symbol-law homogeneity chi2 = 28.2 and Delta-law chi2 = 24.5, both on 28 df (p = 0.45, 0.65).

result.verdict: UNDER-DETERMINED; do not build the SAT/BP solver

entries.coverage: Exact, not estimated. Under the surviving locus P(c_i | p_i, c_prev) = w/(N-s) with w = (1-s) if c_i == c_prev else 1: each rejected draw pins one key value out of N and costs one coin, and p_i does not appear because the plaintext symbol only relabels WHICH key value is pinned and a uniform keystream is invariant under relabelling. Hence P(C|P) is identical for every candidate plaintext, the likelihood over plaintexts is exactly flat, and the acceptance events carry 0 bits about the plaintext. The same line yields the residual doublet rate in closed form, (1-s)/(N-s) = 0.00663779 against an observed 0.00663836 - a third independent route to the filter constant. H(P) is a held-out cross-entropy (an upper bound), so the max-H(K) figure is stated conservatively; sensitivity from 1.5 to 3.0 bits/rune gives max H(K) between 43,183 and 23,749 bits.
not_covered: the zero-information result is conditional on the keystream being uniform and independent of the plaintext; it does not hold if the pad is correlated with the message

the filter IS a leak on the KEY - conditioned on a candidate keystream the skip pattern is constrained at 1/29 per skipped symbol - and that channel is exactly what the beam's validity test already exploits; its size as a ranking channel is measured in R18-L2-SKIP-CHANNEL
the budget assumes the M1 locus; under M2 (value-rewrite) the sampler consumes no extra draws and H(K) drops by 373.6*log2(29) = 1,815 bits, which does not change any verdict

entries.notes: This lane set out to show the filter was unspent information and found the opposite, in closed form. It converges with round17/P4 section 9(3) from the other direction: P4 said a KEY prior buys nothing because the pad has no exploitable non-uniformity; this says an ACCEPTANCE prior buys nothing because the acceptance events are plaintext-independent by construction. The tractability of the derived-key and public-pad lanes comes entirely from the keyspace bound, not from the filter.

corpus/GAPS.md G-09: post times, commit times, file mtimes and PGP signature timestamps exist scattered across sources but no timeline dataset has ever been assembled, and the signature timestamps are recorded in prose only. L8 extension: those timestamps are also a PRIOR over RNG seeds. Round 8 enumerated every unix second of 2011-2015 UNIFORMLY for 10 generators, but seeds are not uniform — a signature time or key-creation time is exactly the kind of number a person types into srand().
entries.$note_on_id: This is the corpus/GAPS.md G-09, not a LEDGER.json id. File as CORPUS-G-09 on merge if the namespace collides.
entries.threshold: Not a hypothesis test — a deterministic derivation with NO search. The derivation set was fixed in PREREG.md and not extended after seeing results: t, t±1, truncation to minute/hour/day, the UTC date as YYYYMMDD and YYYYMMDDHHMMSS, and t in milliseconds. Ranking rule also fixed in advance: provenance_class, then authorship_proximity, then derivation_distance.
entries.result: 433 ranked seed candidates from 59 source timestamps (57 verified: 54 distinct verified signature creation times plus the 7A35090F primary-key, subkey and UID self-sig creation second 1325734783; 2 reported puzzle dates kept separate and ranked last). Tiers: A=54 (verified + author's own machine + the exact second), B=107, C=260, D=12. Highest-ranked candidate is 1325734783 — the second in which the 3301 key, its subkey and its UID self-signature were all created. Handed to L6 / any seed lane as a PRIOR, not a keyspace. THIS LANE RAN NONE OF THEM.
entries.coverage: Every signature-packet creation time in the repository that verifies against 7A35090F, plus the canonical key's own creation timestamps, each carrying per-entry provenance: provenance_class, authorship_proximity, derivation form, the source timestamp it came from, the evidence for it, the source path/URL and a retrieval date.
entries.not_covered: (a) Onion / Tor hidden-service POST times — no authenticated source for any was located, so none is included; they would rank as author_infrastructure if sourced. (b) 4chan and Twitter post times — third-party-recorded, and no archive capture carrying a verifiable second was retrieved. (c) File mtimes inside the held image dumps and the CicadaOS pads — not read here; that is L1-toolchain's surface. (d) The mruzuki key's timestamps are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: nothing ties that key to the author, and including them would smuggle a speculated link into a ranked prior. (e) No seed was executed against any generator — coverage of the candidates themselves is zero by design. (f) Non-seed uses of the timeline (the general chronological dataset G-09 also asks for) are not built here.
entries.reopens_if: A seed lane runs tier A and states which generators and index offsets it covered — at which point tiers B-D are the next bounded increment. Also reopens if an authenticated onion post time or a dated archive capture is recovered, which would add author_infrastructure entries ranking above the present tier D.
entries.notes: CONFOUND DECLARED BEFORE RUNNING (PREREG.md): an RFC 4880 signature creation time is a hashed subpacket taken from the signer's own clock and is therefore settable by the signer. AUDITOR-LOOP-2026-07-28.md used exactly this to REFUTE the timezone/working-hours biometric built on these timestamps (n=26, irreproducible), and that refutation stands — this entry does not reopen it. It also does not weaken this list, because the two uses differ: a spoofed timestamp is worthless as evidence ABOUT A PERSON, but it is still a number the author chose and typed, which is the property that makes it a plausible srand() argument. The distinction was recorded in advance so it could not be invented afterwards to rescue a result.

entries.hypothesis: bash $RANDOM and the glibc random()/rand()/*rand48 family -- ranked 4 (x2) and 1 (x3) by round18/L1-toolchain/RESULTS.md section 6.2 on physical-artifact evidence -- can be reproduced byte-exactly and enumerated as a bounded keystream space for LP2.
entries.coverage: Generator VALIDATION coverage: 19 generators x 8 seeds x 2000 draws vs real libraries, all PASS. Space MEASURED: bash $RANDOM is one orbit per implementation variant (seed IS the state, brand() is a pure map), so seed and keystream-offset are the SAME AXIS for that family; bash4.2 LP64 cycle 2^31-2 (tail 13-72), bash4.2_i32 cycle 343,896 (tail 210k-500k); the auto-seeded path (sbrand(tv_sec ^ tv_usec ^ getpid), variables.c:537) reaches at most 74 * 2^20 = 77,594,624 seeds for a 2012-01..2014-06 run, i.e. 3.6% of 2^31, which is a PRIORITY ORDERING inside the full range. glibc seed space 2^32-1 with no orbit collapse (state 31x32 bits). Measured throughput: 166 beam decodes/s/core (I3 vecbeam), 55 end-to-end with I1+I2, 137,414 rows/s/core for a rigid L=31 9-register head-window screen.
not_covered: NO KEYSTREAM WAS SCORED AGAINST LP2. Phase 0 hold, by design.
bash4.2_i32 has no L1 reference: gcc-multilib absent, so no real 32-bit bash 4.2 binary. The ILP32 model is the same source re-typed with uint32_t/int32_t (level L4).

shuf --random-source is validated against GNU coreutils 9.7, NOT the 8.13 of Ubuntu 12.04; randint_genmax byte-consumption may have changed. Ubuntu 26.04 also ships the Rust uutils shuf as /usr/bin/shuf; G1 prefers /usr/bin/gnushuf.

bash3.2 LP64 orbit is stated analytically, not measured: its map is a full-period LCG mod 2^64 (Hull-Dobell), so Brent would need 2^64 evaluations; the 15-bit output period is 2^31 by the bit-period argument, and the ILP32 sibling measures exactly 2^32 as predicted. Every other bash variant's orbit IS measured (see control_detail.G1-ORB).

bash 4.0/4.1 are only PARTIALLY enumerable: seedrand() re-seeds from gettimeofday^getpid when the state reaches 0, and state 0 IS reachable (RANDOM=2147483647 reaches it in one step). Only the deterministic prefix exists.
openssl enc -k overlaps LEDGER R16-KDF (692,064 configs); the overlap was not computed and S1 must de-duplicate.

lrand48 and Perl-drand48 are round10/L5-seed32/CENSUS.md section B generators 10 and 11, already covered over 2011-2015 unix-seconds; G1 re-implements them only for interface uniformity and S1 must NOT re-sweep that window.
/dev/urandom, bare shuf, `openssl rand`, and bash 5.1's $SRANDOM are UNREACHABLE -- no seed and no record. Not swept, and NO NULL IS REPORTED for them.
The auto-seeded 77.6M subset is an upper bound on the seed SET; the joint distribution of (tv_sec, tv_usec, pid) was not modelled, so the subset cannot yet be ordered by likelihood.

entries.hypothesis: The LP2 keystream is the output of Perl 5.14 `rand` (glibc drand48), seeded explicitly or implicitly via `srand`, reduced to Z_29 by an era-idiomatic Perl form and applied under the pinned soft anti-repeat filter.
entries.coverage: ZERO key-space coverage. This lane swept no seeds and excludes nothing. It delivers: a byte-exact validated generator (9 Perl-reachable reductions + 2 C-only shadow forms), a keystream interface (gen_perl.make_ks), a pre-registered positive-control artifact, a written space statement, and measured throughput. The 9,984 decodes in pilot.json are TIMING DATA, explicitly stamped is_result=false and scores_are_not_findings=true, run on a deliberately arbitrary seed block (base 700,000,000) so they cannot be mistaken for coverage of the high-prior band.
not_covered: every seed -- no seed was scored
per-call or mid-stream re-seeding (srand called more than once)
a keystream offset by an unknown number of rand() draws consumed elsewhere in the same process -- a distinct UNBOUNDED axis, not the same as the sec.4.3 keystream offset
reductions outside the nine enumerated in RESULTS.md sec.2.4
CPAN PRNG modules (Math::Random::MT, Math::Random::Secure) -- a different family, not `rand`
Perl builds configured -Drandfunc=random or -Drandfunc=rand; Configure prefers drand48 on any host that has it, so an Ubuntu 12.04 stock package cannot be one of these, but a hand-built perl could

the 5.14 srand string-coercion column, which is derived from reading pp.c plus documented SvUV semantics and could NOT be executed (no 5.14 runtime available). Residual uncertainty is confined to non-integer srand ARGUMENTS and does not affect coverage, since every coerced value lands inside 0..2^32-1 either way.
entries.reopens_if: Not closed -- not even opened as a sweep. Phase 2 runs it when I1, I2 and I3 publish PASS and G2-GATE-Q1 is executed against plant.json. READY.md sec.4 is the run spec.
entries.result: NO SWEEP RUN -- HELD AT THE SCORING BOUNDARY per the Round 19 campaign plan's hard dependency (Phase 0 gates I1/I2/I3 have not published PASS). What WAS established: (1) VALIDATION PASS -- gen_perl.py reproduces the real perl binary byte-exactly, 186 checks / 0 failing across 3 gates: A = mine vs real perl (164 checks: raw Drand01 at %.17g, int(rand(M)) for M in {26,29,32,100,255,256,1000,2^32} at 13 seeds x 2000 draws, and all 9 reductions driven through real perl loops); B = real perl vs glibc srand48/drand48 from C, 13 seeds x 1024 draws identical to 17 significant digits; C = structural (seed folding, integer-fast-path exactness over 52,000 draws per M, srand() argument coercion). (2) THE ERA QUESTION IS RETIRED BY MEASUREMENT, not argument: this box runs perl 5.40.1, but the perl-5.14.2 tarball (md5 3306fbaf976dcebdcd49b2ac0be00eb9) shows Configure picks drand48 on any glibc host and config_h.SH defines Drand01()=drand48(), seedDrand01(x)=srand48((long)x), RANDBITS=48 -- so 5.14.2 on Ubuntu IS glibc drand48, and gate B measures that leg directly. (3) THE MAIN FINDING -- the space is 2^32 with NO residue, INCLUDING the un-seeded case: util.c Perl_seed() reads sizeof(U32) = FOUR BYTES from /dev/urandom, so `perl -e 'print chr(int(rand(29))) for 1..13000'` with no srand at all has a uniform 32-bit seed and is fully enumerable. (4) Real Phase-2 throughput measured end-to-end through I3 vecbeam + I2 adjudicate: 663 decodes/s/core at L=31, 106/s at L=120; 9,984 pilot decodes emitted 9,984 SWEEPROWs with 0 validate_row failures.

entries.result: FOUND-ERROR. L1 sec.6.2 row 3's 'never swept' is incorrect. round10/L5-seed32/CENSUS.md sec.B lists generator 10 as `Perl srand(S); int(rand(29))`, harness-validated against /usr/bin/perl in VALIDATION.txt (5 seeds x 2000 draws, PASS), and results_newgens.txt records the completed run: `gen=10 perl int(rand(29)) drand48  seeds=1293840000..1420070400  best=-13.4240 @1407171031  hits>-12.5=0  168.1s`. Generator 11 (POSIX lrand48()%29) was run on the same band. A slice HAS been swept. HOWEVER that slice is worth close to nothing on four independently-measured counts: (1) DECODER -- sweep32x.c decode_score() branches over F-nulls only and has no key-skip or drift model at all; it is rigid_decode with an interrupter fork, and round12/D3 measured rigid at -6.835 on the CORRECT key, i.e. noise. Coverage x power ~ coverage x 0. (2) ADJUDICATOR -- English 4-gram only; round18 L7-A measured power 0.33 Latin / 0.00 vowel-dropped English, and no doctrine-R3 language-agnostic statistics were persisted, so the rows are un-reinterpretable. (3) THRESHOLD -- a fixed -12.5 bar, which LEDGER entry B-21 itself calls 'STATISTICALLY INVALID at full-32 scale because the null max grows with trial count'; the reported best -13.42 sits below the bar by less than the null's own spread. (4) BREADTH -- 1 reduction of 9, ~2.9% of the seed space, offset 0 only, no atbash, no sign axis.

entries.hypothesis: The LP2 0-54 keystream was generated INSIDE the typesetting document: by a TeX-side PRNG (pgf's \pgfmathrandominteger, the lcg package's \rand, random.tex's \setrannum, or pdfTeX's \pdfuniformdeviate) invoked from the LaTeX source that produced the 6.00x9.00-inch runic PDF, reduced to Z_29 by one of the idiomatic package calls.
entries.coverage: ZERO decodes of coverage. This is a Phase-1 generator lane: it delivers four byte-exact generators, a keystream interface, and an exact space statement, and it HOLDS at the scoring boundary because Round 19's Phase 0 (I1/I2/I3) had not been certified. A single labelled pilot of 10,000 decodes was run for plumbing and timing only, with `pilot: true, interpretable: false` in its SWEEPROW header; no score in it is interpreted and no candidate was escalated. Anyone citing this entry as coverage of the TeX family is citing it wrongly.
entries.not_covered: Everything. Specifically: (1) the whole 1.85e11-decode space; (2) the lcg package's DEFAULT seed, which depends on \inputlineno and \value{page} as well as the clock - samplable, not enumerable, and not sampled; (3) pdfTeX's DEFAULT seed, set from wall-clock microseconds - not enumerable at all; (4) per-page or per-line reseeding (an author calling \pgfmathsetseed once per page - the B-04 stage-C shape); (5) any constant c not in {0,1} added to the reduced key, i.e. a general Caesar; (6) \pgfmathrandomitem over a declared rune list, which is covered as a STREAM but whose list ordering would impose an unknown alphabet permutation; (7) LuaTeX math.random, which is glibc rand() and therefore G1's space, handed off with its Lua 5.1 scaling rather than re-swept; (8) XeTeX, which had no \uniformdeviate in the TeX Live 2009 era.
entries.reopens_if: Phase 2 (S1) runs it. The gate is K2: a planted phase must survive a 1e-3 rigid prefilter cut in >= 50% of 200 trials. If it does, complete enumeration of the three Lehmer families is ~18 h of wall clock on this box (13 h of numpy prefilter + a beam stage sized by the cut, ~4.4 h at a 1e-6 band-max cut). If it does not, G4 restricts to Tier 1: pgf's 8,627 distinct default seeds (69,016 decodes, 2.0 h at the drift preset on 6 cores), random.tex's 3,214,080 date-init seeds, and 0..2^20 author-typed integers.

pgf.note: the multiplier is 69621, NOT the 16807 the source comment lists as an alternative

lcg.reduction: rejection then first + z mod R

random_tex.reduction: v = (z-1) div (2147483645 div R), rejected unless v < R

pdftex.note: init_randoms halves |seed| until < 2^28, which collapses the seed space to 2^28

result.era_correctness: pgf 2.00 (TeX Live 2009 = Ubuntu 11.04/11.10/12.04) and pgf 2.10 have a byte-identical \pgfmathgeneratepseudorandomnumber; reference vectors from vendored pgf 2.10 match installed pgf 3.1.11a on 76/76.
result.single_cycle_detail: 69621 and 16807 are both primitive roots mod 2^31-1 (verified against every prime factor of 2^31-2 = 2*3^2*7*11*31*151*331); each generator has ONE cycle of length 2147483646, so every seed and every offset is a phase of one master stream. B-04's offset ladder and B-02's key-index-0 assumption are ABSORBED for pgf/lcg/random.tex; they are NOT absorbed for pdfTeX, whose 55-word state gives disjoint trajectories.

entries.result: Of the 29 runes, exactly one -- Y (futhorc 'yr') -- is typeset as two disconnected components: an outline identical to U plus a detached inner stroke of median height 58 px. 54 of 55 sampled Y glyphs carry one; no other rune carries one at all. A segmentation that filters components by rune height therefore discards the stroke and makes every Y in the book pixel-identical to a U (measured ink 2134 vs 2133 on the same 114x53 box). Repairing it moved this lane's bitmap purity from 97.15% to 100.0000% and page agreement from 95.76% to 98.98% in one step.

result.mechanism: max_skip lets the key pointer run AHEAD only. A corrupted cipher rune can induce a spurious skip, after which the beam can never re-synchronise, so derailment compounds with segment length -- the full-book number is the binding one and short-window measurements understate it.
result.consequence: The negatives are not voided: at k=450 the correct key still scores -4.72 against a wrong key's -7.30, so a sweep that RANKS would still surface it. But every sweep in this repo THRESHOLDED, and round18/L2's landmark full-book positive control (-4.098 / recovery 0.9997) is a CLEAN-TRANSCRIPTION result.

entries.hypothesis: The hitfn20 real-mode (no-oracle) clause-3 held-out proxy is a single 1/4->3/4 cut that catches only 15/45 (33%) of correct-key EN_NOVOWEL bar-clearing hallucinations (SYNTHESIS 8.4 FOUND-ERROR). A strengthened proxy that attributes the key phase on each of k disjoint contiguous folds, re-decodes the held-out complement under the same key, and aggregates fold-level rune-index self-consistency by an agreement rule can SEAL the gate: >=0.90 catch on the planted-45 AND on a fresh held-out surrogate, while keeping genuine-decode false-reject <=0.10. No plaintext oracle is used.
entries.threshold: Pre-registered in analysis/round21/L1-seal-realmode-proxy/PREREG.md Q5 BEFORE any measurement on the fold variant. PASS requires ALL of: (P-a) some frozen (k,rule) cell reaches >=0.90 catch on the planted-45 EN_NOVOWEL population (>=41/45); (P-b) the SAME frozen cell holds >=0.90 catch on a fresh held-out surrogate (fresh key seed, disjoint rng offsets); (P-c) genuine-decode false-reject <=0.10 on both tuning and surrogate genuine panels; (P-d) tests/validate.py still passes and SWEEPROW/3 field order unchanged. KILL (declare the no-oracle gate provably leaky, report bar-clearing survivors as flagged-for-oracle): if NO (k,rule) cell reaches >=0.90 catch without genuine false-reject exceeding 0.10. Winning cell chosen by max catch subject to false-reject <=0.10, tie-break smaller k. Threshold not editable after results.
entries.control_detail: Run FIRST, gated everything. (1) Hallucination population reproduced BIT-IDENTICALLY from the S-RESCOPE recipe (Kfull=make_ks('sha256_ctr','mod29',b'CICADA',L*4+1024), L=240, rep in range(60), rng=Random(5000+rep), P=EN_NOVOWEL slice, C=encipher_keyskip(P,Kfull,sign=-1,supp=0.83,seed=600+rep), keep pmax>=bar & true-recovery<0.90): got 45/45. (2) hitfn20 single-cut baseline on those 45 caught EXACTLY 15/45 = 0.333 -- reproduces the FOUND-ERROR being fixed. (3) genuine-decode panel (correct key over EN_MODERN) 20/20 with true recovery >=0.971 (all >=0.95), so the harness demonstrably separates genuine from hallucinated when a proxy can. (4) panelmax_bar exact/1e6 = 7.6341931878728095, unchanged from R19/R20. Both controls PASS => the negative below is a real measured bound, not an unvalidated-instrument null.
